clues.text: This city stands in the southwest of its state, where a tree lined river cuts through dry high desert. Green banks stand out in the brown, dry land.
clues.narrowing: Points to the dry southwest of one mountain state, on a green river valley.

source.quote: Set in a high-desert area, the tree-lined valley of the Boise River became a distinct landmark

clues.text: Days here can bake past 100 in the dry summer heat. Then the nights drop fast, often more than 30 degrees cooler by dawn.
clues.narrowing: Rules out mild coasts; keeps hot, dry towns with cold desert nights.

source.quote: Boise experiences hot and dry summers with highs reaching 100 °F (38 °C) nine days in a typical year

clues.text: This town won the territory capital job in a court fight in 1866. A top court kept the seat here by a single vote.
clues.narrowing: Cuts the list to a capital kept by a one vote court call in 1866.

source.quote: Boise was made the territorial capital of a much reduced Idaho in a controversial decision that overturned a district court ruling by a one-vote majority in the territorial supreme court along geographic lines in 1866.

clues.text: French trappers came on a green, tree lined river in dry country and cried out for the woods. This city's name grew from their French word for wooded land.
clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: one capital took its name from a French word for wooded land.

source.quote: This led the French trappers to call the area " la rivière boisée " ("the wooded river")

clues.text: The governor of Idaho has his office in this city. State lawmakers meet here each year to run the state.
clues.narrowing: Confirms it: the governor and state lawmakers work in this city.

source.quote: is the capital and most populous city in the U.S. state of Idaho

reveal.blurb: Gold finds in 1863 brought a new fort and a rush of miners to this river valley. A court fight then made the young town the territory capital, and it kept the job at statehood. Boise is the capital of Idaho.
